cables.content_gap_shard_title: A shard of this wall has stopped relaying the material it receives. The assembler itself is fine: its inputs are the shards, which re-emit a grain every slot whether their content changed or not — so it CANNOT see the fault. Hence the warning is carried here, on the wall, rather than on a shard folded away in the interface.
cables.content_gap_title: This node relays less new material than it receives: it is recomposing identical frames. The reference is the new-content rate EXPECTED UPSTREAM (source frame rate, propagated stage by stage) — not its own composition rate, which may legitimately be higher. Downstream, which only emits on change, will run at this rate. Check this node's suppliers.

cables.delai.fil_title: Age of the frame going ON THE WIRE: what reaches the sender, plus what emission costs. The last term (1 frame) is a DECLARED constant, not a measurement — hence the ≈. Measurable, see docs/reference/LATENCE_CHAINE.md §6.
cables.delai.incomplet_title: LOWER BOUND: at least one stage on the path does not measure its delay ({s}). The real total is higher.
cables.delai.non_mesure_title: This module does not publish its stage delay. We do not show zero: “no measurement” is not “no delay”.
cables.delai.propage_title: This stage PROPAGATES its source's temporal coordinate (grain opened with src_index=). Under normal operation the gap is zero: that zero is STRUCTURAL, not a re-timing measurement. A NON-ZERO value signals accumulated drift — next_index applies max(candidate, counter+1), so a writer that once ran ahead never comes back down: the grain ships on time, but its CONTENT is that much older. The stage's own cost is on the Load axis.
cables.delai.reception_title: 2110 reception: capture on the wire → shm write (network, MTL framebuffers, de-jitter). This is the FIRST link in the chain and the engine measures it — not processing, but a real delay.

js.txmodel.apply_no_engine: No 2110 engine deployed on this port: nothing to provision.
js.txmodel.apply_over: The model exceeds the port's budget: fix it before applying.
js.txmodel.apply_tip: Sets the port from the chosen model (or the edited layout), then provisions the outputs on the engine — a maintenance event on DPDK (deferral available), free on AF-XDP.
js.txmodel.bind_none: This port comes from no model (layout set by hand, or never set).
js.txmodel.budget_tip: Rate-limiter queues used by the model (1 per video output + 1 per audio flow + 1 per ANC), against THIS PORT's measured ceiling. Each port has its own RL tree and its own ceiling.
js.txmodel.cap_lead: Capturing is READING: the port does not move, nothing is recomputed, nothing is redeployed. The new model will be bound to this port — any future divergence becomes measurable.
js.txmodel.cap_tip: Captures this port's REAL outputs into a new reusable model, pre-bound to its card type. This is a READ: the port is not touched (no tree recompute, no redeployment).
js.txmodel.captured: ✓ model created from this port (the port was not touched)
js.txmodel.commit_3: Wiring a source whose format DIFFERS from the announced one (refused by default: insert a UDC, or realign the output during maintenance)
js.txmodel.commit_title: Costs a tree recompute — the whole port freezes (~2.2 s), on DPDK only
js.txmodel.commit_title_xdp: On this port (AF-XDP): none of this costs anything
js.txmodel.cost_commit_tip: This output will (re)create a video session: one tree rebuild, i.e. a ~1 s freeze of the whole port.
js.txmodel.cost_free_tip: No session to create: nothing to rebuild, no output freezes.
js.txmodel.cost_grow_tip: Beyond the engine's booted budget: “Apply” RECORDS this output but does not create it yet — the output count is frozen in the engine at start-up. It will be created at the next redeploy, which you choose (an alert will remind you until then).
js.txmodel.cost_inert_tip: The engine does not provision that many outputs: this declaration stays inert until an output is added to it (2110 Destinations page).
js.txmodel.d_none: No change: this port is already set exactly like this model.

js.txmodel.diverged: the port has diverged from its model

js.txmodel.empty: No output declared — add one, or load an example.
js.txmodel.expert_tip: Edit THIS port's outputs by hand, off-model. The normal gesture is to apply a library model; manual editing will make the port DIVERGE from its model.
js.txmodel.free_1: Activating a declared output (wiring a source in the announced format)
js.txmodel.free_2: Muting an output (it goes silent again; its pacing leaf stays)
js.txmodel.free_3: Changing an output's source (a plain input swap)

js.txmodel.free_title: Free — live, with no effect on neighbours
js.txmodel.grow_on_apply: The engine currently provisions {n} output(s). Applying this model declares more: the declaration is saved WITHOUT cutting any flow, and takes effect at the engine's next redeploy (flagged by an alert until then).

js.txmodel.impact_no_victim: No output is transmitting on this port right now: the rebuild will go unnoticed.
js.txmodel.impact_none: Nothing to create: applying this model costs no tree rebuild.
js.txmodel.impact_victims: These {n} currently transmitting output(s) will freeze for ~1 s:
js.txmodel.impact_xdp: AF-XDP port: applying this model rebuilds no tree and freezes no output.
js.txmodel.maint_lead: Deferred changes wait here. Apply them right away, schedule them for a time, or drop them from the tray.
js.txmodel.mode_rl_desc: Pacing is done in hardware: declaring an output rebuilds the port's scheduling tree (the WHOLE port stops/restarts for ~1 s — every output on it freezes, including those that asked for nothing). Operating an already-declared output is free.
js.txmodel.mode_xdp_desc: No hardware rate limiter on this port: no tree rebuild, no freeze. Declaring, removing or reformatting an output costs nothing here.
js.txmodel.model_lead: Models are REUSABLE templates defined per CARD TYPE (“2110 card model” tab). Creating them costs nothing; it is HERE, putting them on a real port, that the cost is paid.
js.txmodel.no_compat: No model defined for this card type — create one in the library.
js.txmodel.no_engine: No 2110 engine deployed on this port: the model is stored and will be applied at deployment — nothing to freeze today.
js.txmodel.no_iface: No 2110 media port on this node.

js.txmodel.remove_tip: Remove this output from the model (takes effect when applied).
js.txmodel.save_tip: Saves the declaration only — free, no output moves.
js.txmodel.slots_lead: Every output is declared up front with the format it ANNOUNCES (its SDP contract). The session and its pacing leaf are created at declaration time, at that format's nominal bitrate: wiring a source of the SAME format afterwards costs nothing.

pacing.clock_always: An ST 2110 media card is ALWAYS synchronised — there is no 2110 without a clock. The port mode does not decide whether PTP exists, only WHO carries it.
pacing.clock_conflict: ⚠ ptp4l is currently enabled on this card: saving in DPDK will be REFUSED (binding the card to vfio-pci would kill ptp4l). PTP does not go away though — in DPDK the clock is carried by the engine. Nothing has been changed: it is your call.
pacing.clock_conflict_btn: Stop ptp4l on this card (the engine takes the clock)
pacing.clock_conflict_done: ✓ ptp4l will be removed from this card on save; the clock will be carried by the 2110 engine (libmtl).
pacing.clock_dpdk: The card is bound to vfio-pci: no kernel netdev, no exposed PHC — ptp4l cannot run on it. The 2110 engine embeds its own PTP client (libmtl); that grandmaster is what the emitted SDPs advertise as ts-refclk.
pacing.clock_locked: Not editable in DPDK: ptp4l is impossible on a vfio-pci card.
pacing.clock_none_nic: No card on this node carries ptp4l right now — the node would have no clock.
pacing.clock_other_nic: On this node, {if} already carries ptp4l.
pacing.clock_ptp4l_off: ptp4l does not run on this card: the clock must then be carried by ANOTHER card on the same 2110 network (multi-NIC setup).
pacing.clock_who_other: Carried by ANOTHER card of the network
pacing.clock_who_ptp4l: Carried by ptp4l (kernel, on this card)
pacing.clock_xdp: ptp4l locks to the grandmaster on this card and disciplines its PHC.
pacing.cons_dpdk_clock: PTP clock: carried by the 2110 engine (libmtl) — the card is bound to vfio-pci, ptp4l cannot run on it.
pacing.cons_dpdk_model: TX model: changing it recomputes the pacing tree = the WHOLE PORT stops (~2 s) → maintenance window. Operating it afterwards (enable/mute/reroute) is FREE.
pacing.cons_dpdk_pacing: Hardware pacing: the card runs the rate limiter → the sender profile (narrow) is ACTIVE.
pacing.cons_xdp_clock: PTP clock: carried by ptp4l (kernel daemon, the card's PHC) — the kernel netdev remains.
pacing.cons_xdp_model: TX model: FREE — no rate limiter, hence no tree recompute and no freeze, ever.
pacing.cons_xdp_pacing: Software pacing (TSC): no hardware rate limiter on this port.
pacing.mode_apply: Applied at the node's next 2110 engine (re)deployment.
pacing.mode_lead: The port mode decides EVERYTHING below it: the pacing, who carries the PTP clock, and what the card's TX model costs to apply.
pacing.model_bind_none: This card comes from no model.
pacing.model_confirm: Apply the model to this card
pacing.model_cost_dpdk: In DPDK, applying a model recomputes the pacing tree: the whole port stops for ~2 s. Outputs are therefore declared AHEAD of time, in a maintenance window; afterwards, enabling, muting or re-sourcing a declared output costs nothing.
pacing.model_cost_xdp: In AF-XDP, applying a model costs NOTHING: no rate limiter, hence no tree recompute and no output freeze.
pacing.model_lead: The card's real outputs, the model choice and its application live in the “This card's 2110 outputs” panel, at the bottom of this page.
pacing.model_none: No model compatible with this card type — create one on the “2110 card models” page (you can capture it from the card itself).
pacing.pmd_hint: The port mode decides the real pacing: AF-XDP = software TSC; DPDK = the card's hardware rate limiter (narrow baseline). Applied at the node's next 2110 engine deployment.
pacing.profile_hint: ST 2110-21 sender profile per media interface. Narrow = hardware RL (compliant, ≤ 63 video senders/port); Wide = TSC (looser, interop/long-haul). Default: Narrow.

settings.alarms.crashloop.desc: A script that keeps dying is restarted with an increasing delay (backoff), then quarantined (crash-loop status, no more auto-restart) with its last logs in the alert. Leave quarantine with a manual restart.

settings.alarms.signal.desc: The 2110 engine detects black picture, frozen picture and audio silence on its inputs (Rx) and wired outputs (TX). Alert on appearance, info on recovery. Requires engine ≥ 0.37.0.
settings.alarms.signal.title: Signal presence
settings.alarms.title: On-air alarms
settings.alarms.webhook.desc: JSON POST to a URL of your choice (Slack/Teams/Mattermost/n8n/in-house monitoring…) on every alert at or above the chosen level. Without it the whole alerting chain is pull-only: a human must open a page to discover an outage. Disabled by default.
settings.alarms.webhook.state_off: Sending disabled or URL not set — no alert leaves this system.
settings.alarms.webhook.title: Webhook (push output)
settings.alerting.ntfy.desc: Sends alerts as PUSH notifications to the team's phones (ntfy apps for iOS and Android). A batch of alerts becomes ONE notification carrying the count, with a direct link to the incident log.
settings.alerting.ntfy.group_help: A phone is the channel that most needs grouping: forty notifications in a row are not forty pieces of information, they are a phone set to silent — and the next real failure with it. Severity drives ntfy priority: an error goes out at urgent priority, which cuts through Do Not Disturb.
settings.alerting.ntfy.public_warn: PUBLIC server with no token: the topic name is then the ONLY secret protecting your alerts. Anyone who guesses it reads your installation's topology and failures. Choose a long, unguessable name, add a token, or host ntfy on your own site — the only defensible production setup.
settings.alerting.ntfy.title: ntfy channel (push notification)
settings.alerting.ntfy.token_kept: A token is stored and shown masked. To REPLACE it, click the field and type the new one — the old one is never asked for. To keep it, leave it alone.
settings.alerting.snmp.desc: Sends ONE SNMPv3 notification per alert to an NMS, with its context as varbinds (kind, severity, node, container, production slot, message key). Emission is delegated to the SNMP service, which owns the MIB and the OIDs.
settings.alerting.snmp.help: The test is synchronous and ignores the switch above. It sends the current form, EXCEPT the passphrases: the stored ones are used, as a secret has no business travelling through the browser for a test.
settings.alerting.snmp.no_window: No grouping window for this channel: it is forced to 0, one notification per alert. Aggregating several alerts into one send would destroy correlation at the NMS — and the product's own debounce already guards against storms, upstream.
settings.alerting.snmp.secret_help: 8 characters minimum (RFC 3414) and the two passphrases must differ. They are never returned by the server: leaving the mask keeps the stored ones.
settings.alerting.snmp.secret_kept: A passphrase is stored and shown masked. To REPLACE it, click the field and type the new one — the old one is never asked for. To keep it, leave it alone.
settings.alerting.snmp.title: SNMP channel (v3 notifications)
settings.alerting.snmp.trap_engine: In trap mode the SENDER is authoritative: the receiver must know OUR engine ID, or it discards the trap without a word. Provision it on the NMS (net-snmp: createUser -e 0x…) —
settings.alerting.snmp.trap_warn: A trap is NOT acknowledged: a notification lost in transit is lost with no sign of it, neither here nor at the NMS. Choose it only for an NMS that will not accept informs — otherwise keep « inform ».
settings.alerting.syslog.desc: Sends every alert to the collector as RFC 5424, one line per event, with structured data (kind, container, node) that the collector can filter on.
settings.alerting.syslog.help: The test is synchronous and ignores the switch above: you must be able to validate the settings before enabling the channel. It sends what is currently typed in, not the saved configuration.
settings.alerting.syslog.title: Syslog channel (RFC 5424)
settings.alerting.syslog.udp_warn: UDP guarantees nothing: an alert lost on the way is lost WITH NO SIGN AT ALL, neither here nor at the collector. Pick it only for a collector that accepts nothing else — otherwise TCP or TLS.

Yet part of operations happens in a table, where a single card carries N rows of three controls — and sixteen slots at control-surface metrics push the card off screen. This class goes on the CONTAINER: what it holds tightens up, nothing else changes. The touch target is not sacrificed.

A plugin picks a variant and cites it by class; it does not redefine it privately. Genuinely unique things (the mixer T-bar, the PiP composer) stay with their plugin.
settings.controls.knob_hint: Continuous adjustment. The value stays legible: knowing the position is not enough. Variants only change the drawing; colours and states are shared.

settings.controls.meter_hint: They report, they are not operated. Segmented rather than continuous, so they stay legible in greyscale.

settings.cpu_alerts.antirebond_hint: seconds — a repeating symptom writes one line, then a counted summary; 0 disables
settings.cpu_alerts.cadence_hint: Compares each container's OBSERVED fps against its TARGET rate. This is the most direct signal: it measures the outcome, not a cause. A 60 s grace period follows any start or restart (fps is a rolling window: a dip right after a deploy is an artefact).
settings.cpu_alerts.clear_ratio_hint: fraction of target required to close the episode (0.98 = 98%)
settings.cpu_alerts.clear_samples_hint: how long the rate must hold before closing (12 ≈ 60 s)
settings.cpu_alerts.disk_margin_hint: percentage points below the alert threshold
settings.cpu_alerts.flap_hint: A source that keeps toggling is ONE incident, not a hundred. Past the flap count below, a single “unstable source” alert is raised, then that slot's transitions stop being notified until it settles.
settings.cpu_alerts.intro: When CPU runs short, the orchestrator alerts on TRANSITION (no repeats; only an escalation re-alerts). These thresholds drive the three detectors. Leave a field empty to restore its default.
settings.cpu_alerts.psi_cont_hint: Share of time ALL the container's tasks are stalled waiting for a core. On a healthy node this is ~0. At 50 fps, 10 % means 2 ms of budget lost before any compute happens. A CPU-usage percentage cannot tell “busy and healthy” from “suffocating” — PSI can.
settings.cpu_alerts.psi_host_hint: Share of time at least one task on the node is waiting for a core.
settings.cpu_alerts.retention_hint: rows kept — the feed doubles as the “who did what” journal
settings.cpu_alerts.stable_hint: seconds without a flap before notifications resume
settings.cpu_alerts.title: CPU alert thresholds
settings.ctl.bus_solid_d: The gallery standard: the button is the bus.
settings.ctl.bus_tally_d: Colour at the head, the button body neutral.
settings.ctl.dense_d: Goes on a CONTAINER, not on a control: whatever it holds takes table metrics, without changing markup, states or drawing. For surfaces where one card carries N rows of controls (slots of a 2110 engine, tracks of a recorder). The 44 px touch target is KEPT, through .btn-sm's pseudo-element grab area — vertical only, so that two neighbouring controls do not steal each other's finger.
settings.ctl.dotid_d: Carries an element's COLOUR and ties it to the preview. Distinct from the LED, which states a status. Stacked in .ctl-dots, they overlap: a multiple selection reads as a group.
settings.ctl.gauge_d: A bounded value read as a MARGIN. The line materialises the alert threshold. RULE: the value floats on hover, but stays displayed permanently in warn, in over and when the measurement is missing — hovering is not possible with a finger, and it is when things go wrong that one wants the figure without hunting for it.
settings.ctl.knob_arc_d: The most informative: position and value read together.
settings.ctl.knob_collar_d: The most legible from a distance, like a control-surface encoder.
settings.ctl.knob_gate_d: Set and mute in one place: the central indicator is a button in its own right.
settings.ctl.knob_needle_d: Compact. The exact position is hard to guess without the figure.
settings.ctl.knob_thick_d: The plainest, and the most discreet too.
settings.ctl.led_d: Outside a pushbutton, the LED states a STATUS that the click does not toggle — the typical case is a button that OPENS a window. Its tint comes from a token, and --ctl-led-col makes it come from the status vocabulary when it is one. It is never enough on its own: the label states the function.
settings.ctl.meter_d: Segmented, never continuous: stays legible in greyscale.
settings.ctl.mixed_d: When several elements are selected, a setting that differs from one to the next is flagged — without it the field shows a value that belongs to nobody. The border is caught while scanning, the ≠ sign NAMES the reason. Goes on the control or on its wrapper. Touching a mixed setting either uniformises it (appearance) or offsets it (geometry).
settings.ctl.push_engraved_d: The idea of a recessed button, with no relief at all.
settings.ctl.push_led_d: The state reads twice over, discreet and consistent with the rest of the console.
settings.ctl.readout_d: Exact and editable, aligned with the console's fields.
settings.ctl.rule_d: Position on a bounded scale, with the value spelled out.
settings.ctl.seg7_d: Reads from further away than a readout; cannot be edited.
settings.ctl.seg7lit_d: EXCEPTION: halo and status red. Reserved for values that are REALLY in alarm.
settings.ctl.select_d: Choose from a CLOSED, known set (preset, source, mode). The arrow is drawn by the catalogue, otherwise it changes look from one machine to the next.
settings.ctl.strips_d: One column per channel. The 1px hairline is the separator.
settings.ctl.switch_d: A boolean SETTING one sets and reads back. Never a bare checkbox. To be told apart from the pushbutton, which commands an operational action.
settings.ctl.toolbar_d: Align, size, distribute. The group states the family of action; `.ctl-tool.on` marks a tool that TOGGLES. Icons and construction: MXLControls.ICONS / .toolGroup().

settings.doc.100_sources_pre_initialisee: 100 pre-initialised sources · project · sorting, filtering, auto-increment, copy-paste · live tally.
settings.doc.adresse_flottante_que_visen: Floating address the operators point at. It fails over automatically: the VRRP priority is derived from the role (a promotion/demotion moves it), and if the orchestrator stops answering, the other controller takes it over within seconds. Control itself stays manual: after a failure the VIP leads to a read-only controller — that is intended, it is the page carrying the “Promote” button. Configure it on both machines, with the same address, the same VRRP id and the same secret.
settings.doc.agent_deja_installe_pour_un: Agent already installed — for a node that already runs bobi-node-agent but never announced itself (installed without a token, isolated segment…). Enter its host and its agent token; the orchestrator probes its API (/v1/capabilities) and fills in images, network, NICs and capabilities on its own. No root SSH.
settings.doc.attention_ecrase_la_db_cour: Warning: this overwrites the current DB. An automatic backup of the present state is created under backups/ before overwriting.
settings.doc.bascule_manuelle_promouvoir: Manual switchover: promoting a standby applies the last replica it received to its DB and restarts it as active. Anti-split-brain order: demote the active one → promote the standby (the VIP follows on its own if keepalived is configured below, otherwise move it by hand — see HA.md).
settings.doc.bibliotheque_des_cartes_med: Library of 2110 media NICs measured on the bench (narrow TX RL capacity, PTP, DDP). The measured profile takes precedence over the static library at deployment. Qualification reads the 2110_io engine running on the node; narrow_ok requires a loopback probe (manual bench measurement).
settings.doc.carte_des_cpus_visible_cote: CPU map as seen from the host —. Green cells = pinning defined, orange = conflict (two containers target the same core), grey = free CPU.
settings.doc.ce_token_sert_aussi_de_secr: This token ALSO serves as the secret for HA replication — in that case it must be identical on both controllers (copy it, do not regenerate it).
settings.doc.cette_valeur_doit_etre_rigo: ⚠ This value must be strictly identical on both controllers: the active one presents it, the standby compares it with its own. Generate it here, then copy it into this same field on the other machine (the field stays reachable on a read-only standby). It is the same secret as the update token (“Update between instances” section) — a single setting.
settings.doc.chaque_type_de_container_es: Every container type is a plugin (plugins/<type>/). “Reload” re-scans the folder hot (without restarting the service). Drift = containers deployed against a manifest version older than the current one: “Redeploy” brings them up to date.
settings.doc.colonnes_0_et_1_sont_automa: Columns 0 and 1 are automatic (Hostname and MXL, from the linked source). Columns 2-9 can be renamed freely.
settings.doc.copie_coherente_de_db_bobis: A consistent copy of db_bobistudio.db into backups/ once a day, at the time given (server local time). Only the most recent ones are kept.
settings.doc.defaut_selon_l_installation: Default for the installation. Each source's SDP takes precedence (a=ptime, automatic per input); this setting is only a fallback when the SDP does not state it. A wrong ptime makes every packet be dropped (“pkt len mismatch”). Applied at the MTL engine's redeploy.
settings.doc.deux_couches_distinctes_orc: Two distinct layers: Orchestrators (the code, between Bobi.Studio instances on the network) and Nodes (the runtime Docker images, towards the cluster hosts).
settings.doc.elles_visent_select_une_cas: They target select, a checkbox or a .ctl-* class and redefine its appearance. The typical case is the background shorthand, which resets background-image and therefore erases the arrow of .ctl-select: the list stops announcing that it has options. Geometry (widths, margins) remains legitimate — it belongs to the plugin. To be reviewed, not necessarily fixed: an override coming from base.css is not seen here.
settings.doc.genere_un_paquet_zip_avec_l: Generates a package (zip) with the chosen plugins and services. This build is this instance's version: it is what gets installed on a New server and pushed/pulled between Fleet instances. The zip holds code only (never config_local.py nor the databases).
settings.doc.herite_pilotage_par_ssh_roo: Legacy: driven over ssh root@<host> (passwordless key). Avoid it for a new node: prefer the agent, which removes root SSH.
settings.doc.i_le_reseau_de_controle_ip_: ℹ The control network (IP/NIC) and the storage are set at the next step (after the token is created), together with the installation mode.
settings.doc.i_tout_ce_qui_depend_du_mat: ℹ Everything that depends on the hardware is set after enrolment (container network, PTP/hugepages for io2110), once the agent has reported its NICs.
settings.doc.images_partagees_des_conten: Shared container images (bobi-compute: compute; bobi-media: player/recorder/transcoder; bobi-webrtc: gateway). Built once on the host chosen below, then distributed automatically to every node that runs them (by capability). bobi-mtl (ST 2110 / E810) is built per node against that node's NIC (MTL clone + NIC). “Build all” = compute + media.
settings.doc.laisser_vide_dans_la_plupar: Leave empty in most cases: the controller pushes the images to the node itself at enrolment. Fill it in only if you already run your own registry.
settings.doc.le_changement_de_role_prend: ⚠ The role change takes effect at the next restart of the service (hot switchover comes with promote — B3-2c).
settings.doc.le_detail_des_multiviews_sh: The detail of sharded multiviews (full path sources → shards → assembler, formats and latencies) is under Monitoring → Multiview detail.
settings.doc.liste_des_formats_proposes_:
List of formats offered in the container deployment palette, meant for receiving ST 2110-20 broadcast flows.
One format per line, ; separated: Name; Width; Height; FPS; Scan; Chroma; BitDepth; Colorimetry
Scan = p (progressive) / i (interlaced) · Chroma = 420 / 422 / 444 (default 422) · BitDepth = 8 / 10 / 12 (default 10) · Colorimetry = 709 / 2020 / 2020pq / 2020hlg / 601 (default 709)
Fields after Scan are optional (older 5-field lines remain valid).
settings.doc.met_a_jour_le_code_entre_in: Updates the code between Bobi.Studio instances on the network (secrets, databases and uploads are never transferred). My version: —.
settings.doc.mtl_dpdk_exige_un_noyau_val: MTL/DPDK requires a validated kernel (6.14 on the reference stack); the default Debian kernel may not do. Set here, this package is installed automatically when an io2110 node enrols (reboot required). Leaving it empty = no pinning (the installer only warns). It does not affect compute/media/webrtc nodes.
settings.doc.nombre_de_grains_conserves_:
Number of grains held simultaneously in each shared buffer (/dev/shm). This parameter is injected at every container redeploy; existing containers keep running with the value they were deployed with.
Increasing the video ring absorbs ST 2110 network jitter better, at the cost of extra shared RAM.
Range 2 to 8: MTL mode (st20) caps the ring at 8.
settings.doc.outils_requis_pour_monter_l: Tools required to mount the Media Manager's external shares. Checked/installed on the orchestrator itself (that is where the shares are mounted): cifs-utils (SMB) and nfs-common (NFS).
settings.doc.plage_de_groupes_multicast_: Range of multicast groups the orchestrator allocates (cluster-unique) to 2110 flows with no imposed address. Existing flows keep their multicast (no automatic reassignment).
settings.doc.plan_management_ci_dessus_i: Management plane (above, for information: where the control path and the :9100 agents live). The container plane = the IP pool below (put the private range there when separate); the container VLAN is set per node (the node's NIC). IPAM is centralised (the orchestrator assigns every container's IP).
settings.doc.pour_un_autre_hote_source_p: For another source host: prefix with BOBI_BASE=http://…:5000.
settings.doc.pre_selectionne_automatique: Pre-selected automatically in the deployment palette for new containers. The list updates when the formats above are saved.
settings.doc.quand_un_multiview_sature_s: When a multiview saturates (its own latency exceeds the frame budget), the orchestrator automatically splits it into several parallel shards + an assembler (transparent: same output), and restores it as a monolith when the load drops. Applies only to compute Docker nodes (not LXC). It also shares common pieces between multiviews.
settings.doc.quand_une_source_deja_cable: When a source already cabled to a TX output changes format in operation (a camera switches), the system alerts first, then inserts a converting UDC to restore the announced format — changing an output's source is a plain swap: no other output is touched. Unchecking silences nothing: the alert stays, only the insertion becomes manual.
settings.doc.ram_video_n_resolution_2_ex: Video RAM ≈ N × resolution × 2 — e.g. 8 × 1080p YUV422 ≈ —
settings.doc.refuse_un_cable_dont_la_sou: Rejects a cable whose source is incompatible with the consumer (resolution, chroma, rate), with a message explaining why — instead of producing an unreadable picture. Converters (UDC/Multiviewer) and auto-detecting consumers are exempt. Uncheck to fall back to a plain warning (non-blocking).
settings.doc.reglages_de_niveau_cluster_: Cluster-level settings (system-wide): VMID range, network planes (management / containers / 2110 multicast) and high availability. Per-node hardware preparation (Ethernet/SR-IOV/PTP, CPU) lives under Nodes & Hardware.
settings.doc.replication_d_etat_actif_st: State replication (active → standby): the active controller periodically pushes a consistent SQLite snapshot to the standby, which stages it (without applying it — applying = manual switchover, B3-2c). Leaving the URL empty disables replication.
settings.doc.role_de_ce_controleur_dans_: Role of this controller within a pair. Active: drives everything (node monitoring, NMOS/Ember+/ATEM/TSL services, PTP sampler, backup). Standby: boots passive — UI is read-only, drives nothing — waiting for a manual switchover. Prevents split-brain when a 2nd controller is running.
settings.doc.services_qui_tournent_dans_: Services running inside the orchestrator (services/<name>/). Click a row to expand its versions. A version change takes effect at the service's next restart.
settings.doc.simple_management_conteneur: Simple: management + containers on a single network (small systems, = current behaviour). Separate: management network + dedicated private container network (trunked VLAN, /16 outside the gallery LAN — large systems; the orchestrator must be multi-homed on both). The ST 2110 plane always stays physically separate (SR-IOV — see Network → ST 2110).
settings.doc.subnet_passerelle_pool_d_ip: Subnet / gateway / IP pool = cluster (below). The macvlan parent NIC and the VLAN (only if the NIC is a trunk port) are set per node — Deployment → Nodes → ⚙ Configuration.
settings.doc.suivre_le_format_stocke_les: “Follow the format” stores 10/12-bit frames on 16 bits: ×2 shm memory and bandwidth. “Force 8 bits” preserves current performance. Applied at each container redeploy.
settings.doc.telecharge_le_fichier_db_bo: Downloads the db_bobistudio.db file as it stands on the server. The file holds containers, projects, layouts, settings and users.

settings.doc.un_jeton_un_serveur_en_atte: A token = a server waiting to be installed. Create it, then select it and choose an installation mode (USB, iLO, UEFI HTTP). The token stays here until it has been used; the selection survives a page reload.
settings.doc.un_nud_un_hote_qui_execute_: A node = a host that runs the pipeline's containers. The orchestrator drives it through its agent (token API, port 9100). Containers are then created from the usual palette (Containers page), which offers a node selector.

settings.doc.une_sortie_tx_annonce_un_fo: A TX output announces a format in its SDP. Cabling a source of another format to it would make it emit something other than what it announces (not ST 2110 compliant) and would recreate its session: on a rate-limited NIC the port's transmit tree is re-timed and every output on the card freezes for ~1 s. settings.mcast.intro: Multicast addresses for ST 2110 flows: cluster-wide global pool, with optional strict rules per logical network or per physical interface — useful when a switch only relays certain ranges on certain ports (IGMP snooping / static forwarding).
settings.mcast.plan_help: Addressing plan: one multicast group PER FLOW, derived from its rank (base + essence offset + output number). An IGMP subscription targets the GROUP, not the port — two flows differing only by port cannot be told apart by a receiver. Empty = default convention (video .1, .2… / ANC .51, .52… / 1st audio .101, .102… / 2nd audio .201, .202…).

settings.mcast.rules_hint: An Interface rule overrides the Network rule for that port. A rule with format criteria (scan/resolution/fps, audio channels) only applies to flows matching those criteria exactly; without criteria, it applies to the whole essence.
settings.mv.clock_tz_help: Leave on « Wall time zone » to follow the system setting. Picking a city lets one wall show several zones.
settings.mxl.engine_cpu_help: The limiting factor for an engine core is the packet rate it must process (depends on the machine's CPU and memory bandwidth). The quota below is THE calibration knob: the engine fills each core up to this rate before spilling to the next one, and the number of reserved cores is sized with the same value. Applied when the engine is redeployed.
settings.mxl.history_derived_audio_lbl: Audio depth (×2 — the SDK only reads half the buffer at a time):
settings.mxl.history_help: How long a lagging reader can still read a flow before its slot gets recycled; the depth in frames follows from it (duration × frame rate, shown below). PER-NODE setting — the MXL SDK ignores this option when set at the container level — and only applies to flows created AFTERWARDS, not to ones already open.
settings.mxl.history_warn: ⚠ below the SDK default (200 ms): less margin to absorb network jitter, with no measured benefit in return — this setting does not save RAM. The depth shown above is what you will be left with.
settings.mxl.log_level_hint: “Warnings” (default) keeps the engine logs readable: from “Info” upwards, libmtl periodically prints a bulky statistics dump that drowns everything else. Verbose levels are for one-off diagnostics only — switch back to “Warnings” afterwards. Applied when the engine is redeployed.
settings.mxl.pin_cores_hint: Reserves the engine's DPDK cores in the allocator (never handed to pinned compute containers) and confines the engine container to those cores + 2 cores for its controller. Automatic safeguard if the machine lacks cores.
settings.mxl.ring_video_hint: (2110 engine framebuffers, RX and TX — 6 to 8, default 8. Below that the TX repeats frames: measured at 1 in 4 with 4 framebuffers)
settings.mxl.sch_quota_hint: Conservative: 2500 ≈ 2× 1080p50 streams per core. Too high packs too many streams per core (sessions may freeze under load); too low wastes cores. Tune per machine (watch the SCH "avg loop" in the engine logs).
settings.mxl.shm_pipeline: SHM pipeline — theoretical bitrate per container
settings.mxl.slice_help: Grains are published band by band rather than whole-frame: each stage starts on the first band instead of waiting for the full image. This is an MXL bus granularity, like the history depth above.
settings.mxl.slice_hint: ⚠ Yields nothing if a single stage does not slice — one monolithic producer in the middle cancels the benefit of all the others, and you pay for slicing without gaining latency. Measured 2026-08-11: a pyramide left whole-frame cost ONE frame to the entire chain. Takes effect on each container's (RE)DEPLOYMENT: already-deployed containers keep their state. Check: mxl-info on a flow → "Commit batch size" greater than 1.

settings.net.clocks_alerts: Alert when a node leaves the grid
settings.net.clocks_common: All nodes move away from the reference the same way (%s): look at the REFERENCE itself, or at the measurement path — a common movement does not come from each of them separately.
settings.net.clocks_ctrl_t: The orchestrator writes no MXL flow: its clock need not be on the media grid. It is shown because it mediates the measurement — its drift would appear on every row had it been used as the reference.
settings.net.clocks_desc: The MXL bus indexes its grains on time: two nodes that do not land on the same grid can neither align their flows nor replicate them. The only clock that matters is CLOCK_TAI — the one libmxl reads.
settings.net.clocks_drift_t: Rate at which this node moves away from the REFERENCE (the node locked to the grandmaster), over the history window. Repeatability ± %s ms. The measurement bias, common to both, cancels in the difference: drift shows up here even if the absolute position stays uncertain. A value on the order of the repeatability means zero.
settings.net.clocks_far: usable, but far from the grid
settings.net.clocks_far_help: Beyond half a grain (%s ms here), a node synced to this server no longer designates the same frame as its peers.
settings.net.clocks_gap_t: Measured by the node agent using NTP's four-timestamp model, with node-side processing removed: this column resolves to a fraction of a millisecond. Raw: %s
settings.net.clocks_gm_free: free-running grandmaster (clockClass %s) — locked, but onto a worthless reference
settings.net.clocks_judge: An NTP server can claim “stratum 1” and be wrong: the rank states its claim, not its accuracy. The node locked to the grandmaster therefore acts as JUDGE — it compares the server against the site's real time reference. A gap beyond one grain disqualifies it for a compute node, whatever its rank.
settings.net.clocks_nojudge: no PTP judge available (no node locked to a grandmaster)
settings.net.clocks_ntp_help: One or more servers, space-separated. A common source makes nodes comparable: two different servers are two ideas of time, and their gap shows up between nodes with no way to tell where it came from. No effect on a 2110 node, whose time comes from the grandmaster. Empty = leave everything as is.
settings.net.clocks_ntp_ko: chrony ACCEPTED this server then DISCARDED it: it disagrees with the other sources (%s). A stratum 1 server can be wrong — the rank states its claim, not its accuracy. Check the server, or make it exclusive so it has no contradictor (at the risk of following a wrong clock).
settings.net.clocks_ok: The whole cluster is on the same grid
settings.net.clocks_ref_t: Cluster reference: the best-traceable node. Offsets are expressed RELATIVE TO IT, which cancels the controller's own drift.
settings.net.clocks_test_none: Enter one or more servers, then “Test”: each candidate is queried from the controller, from every node, and judged by the node locked to the grandmaster.
settings.net.clocks_thr_help: Left at 0, the threshold is DERIVED from the node's job: half a grain for a compute node (beyond that it designates the neighbouring frame), a microsecond for a node pacing ST 2110 packets. The rate comes from the default video format, floored at 60 fps — between 50 and 60 the difference is slim, so take the more constraining one. A non-zero value overrides the derivation on every node.
settings.net.clocks_trap: On a 2110 node, host probes (systemctl, ps, timedatectl) all report “no clock” — this is WRONG. The discipliner is libmtl, inside the engine container, visible neither as a service nor as a process. Always read the engine's environment before concluding.
settings.net.clocks_tz_xref: This section configures clock SYNCHRONISATION. To choose the displayed time zone:
settings.net.clocks_uncert: The TAI offset is measured by the node agent's clock endpoint (≥ 0.18.0): four timestamps, connection established BEFORE the stopwatch starts, node-side processing taken out of the equation — hence an uncertainty of %s instead of the ± 25 ms the old shell probe cost. This column now resolves grain-level agreement, not just gross errors (missing kernel offset, absent source, inconsistent convention). Local accuracy sampled on each node remains the reference measure for discipline quality, in microseconds.
settings.net.clocks_within_t: Offset indistinguishable from zero at the measurement resolution (%s)
settings.net.cluster_desc: Cluster map: the orchestrator and the nodes, their interfaces (role, IP) and their cabling. Control links the orchestrator to each node's management; every media2110 NIC joins the red or blue fabric of its 2110 network.
settings.net.guide_2110: The ST 2110 pipeline runs over MTL (DPDK/AF-XDP). Prefer Intel E810 (ice driver, validated path). ConnectX-4+ (mlx5) works; ConnectX-3 (mlx4) is not supported. Dedicate a PF to media, give it an IP, and pair red/blue for SMPTE 2022-7.
settings.net.guide_connector: Optical (SFP/QSFP) for long or inter-rack links. DAC (direct-attach copper) for short intra-rack runs: cheaper, low latency/power. RJ45 = management/control. Click an optical connector to see Tx/Rx levels (DOM).
settings.net.guide_ptp: Require hardware timestamping (E810 and ConnectX-4+). Domain 127 (SMPTE 2059-2 profile). One JBOD clock per domain, single BMCA; the primary domain disciplines the system clock.
settings.net.guide_rdma: Mellanox RoCE (mlx5) is the most mature and robust. Intel irdma (E810) works but is more fragile (e.g. conflicts with changing ethtool channels, must be disabled for some ops). If RDMA is critical → ConnectX; the E810 shines mostly for 2110.
settings.net.orch_no_route: The orchestrator has neither an IP nor a route to the container subnet {net} → it will not be able to reach the containers.

settings.net.ptp_graphs_hint: Each node synchronizes to the grandmaster independently — pick the network then the node to plot. Both curves describe the NIC clock (the SLAVE port's PHC) against the grandmaster: offset and mean path delay. The gap between the node's SYSTEM clock and the NIC clock (phc2sys) is a different measurement — shown under the offset on a ptp4l node, not yet published by the engine PTP.

A link is created before its source format is read: the allocator falls back to this value, then corrects itself on the next re-establishment. Better to overestimate (spread out) than underestimate (pile up). Reference: a 1080p50 4:2:2 flow is ~1.7 Gb/s at 8-bit, ~2.1 Gb/s at 10-bit.

settings.sap.announced_help: Our 2110 outputs rebroadcast on the SAP group. Ticking an output makes it visible — and therefore subscribable — to third-party receivers. The SDP we broadcast is the IS-05 transport file, the one carrying the real grandmaster. Unticking sends a deletion packet so the entry disappears on their side too.
settings.sap.bind_help: 239.255.255.255 is the address used by the audio world (AES67, Ravenna, Dante); 224.2.127.254 is the RFC one. The local address decides which interface we speak on: left empty on a controller with several legs, the kernel would pick the default route — the control LAN — and the announcements would never reach the media plane.
settings.sap.discovered_help: What third-party equipment announces on the groups we listen to. The verdict checks each stream against what the 2110_io engine can actually receive (L24 / 48 kHz / 8 channels, ST 2110-30 ptime) and against our clock. The PTP domain is the classic Dante-in-AES67-mode trap: it usually comes out on domain 0 while a 2110 plant runs on 127.
settings.sap.intro: SAP (RFC 2974) is the discovery mechanism shared by AES67, Ravenna and Dante in AES67 mode: a sender periodically broadcasts its SDP to a multicast group, a receiver listens on that group and subscribes to what it sees there. None of this equipment speaks NMOS — without a SAP announcement, none of it can subscribe to our streams. SAP travels on the media plane: the controller needs a leg on it, and a 2110 port bound to vfio-pci (DPDK) no longer has a netdev, so it stays out of reach.
settings.sap.none_discovered: No stream announced on the groups we listen to.
settings.sap.none_senders: No 2110 output declared — nothing to announce.

settings.securite.pwd_retro: Applies only to passwords entered AFTERWARDS. Existing passwords are not re-checked: they are stored as hashes, so unreadable — tightening the profile cannot invalidate them retroactively.
settings.securite.pwd_souple_d: 8 characters, a single kind of character is enough. For an installation with no route out and controlled physical access.

settings.securite.pwd_toujours: In all three cases these stay refused: a common password, reuse of the username or name, a keyboard run. They cost a good-faith user nothing and they are an attack's first attempts.

wiz.node.card.later: The 2110 interfaces (media-plane IP, roles, PMD, 2110 network, PTP) are configured once the node is enrolled, on Settings → Network → Interfaces — all at once, with the topology in view. Nothing to do here now.
wiz.node.card.lead: Nothing to set here: 2110 interfaces are configured after enrollment.
wiz.node.card.title: ST 2110 interfaces
wiz.node.docker.lead: Docker runs the node's containers. If it isn't installed yet, install it here (1–2 min).
wiz.node.docker.title: Docker (host)
wiz.node.done.lead: Summary of the node's state. Is everything green? Otherwise go back to the relevant step with "Back".
wiz.node.done.title: Done
wiz.node.hostprep.lead: Reserves 1 GB hugepages and enables IOMMU + vfio, required by the ST 2110 pipeline. "Apply" changes the kernel boot command line: a host reboot is then required. The default count (16 = 16 GB) suits most cases.
wiz.node.hostprep.title: Host preparation (MTL / ST 2110)
wiz.node.images.lead: Checks that the Docker images this node requires are present. bobi-mtl builds on the node; compute/media are pushed from the Build tab.
wiz.node.images.title: Runtime images
wiz.node.network.lead: Pick the "parent" network card that will carry the containers (container address plan). Subnet and gateway come from the cluster settings.
wiz.node.network.title: Container network (macvlan)
wiz.node.not_done: not complete yet — apply the action above then verify again
wiz.node.ok_confirmed: all good, this step is complete
wiz.node.queues.lead: Enables all of the E810 card's queues for the MTL AF-XDP pipeline (one 2110 session = one queue). Required on a 2110 node: without it the engine fails with "no free queue found" and no stream is received.
wiz.node.queues.title: NIC queues (AF-XDP)
wiz.node.queues_not_done: not all NIC queues active — click "Enable all queues" above, otherwise the MTL engine finds no queue ("no free queue found") and no stream arrives
wiz.node.reboot_back: the node is back and the preparation is active
wiz.node.reboot_required: A host reboot is required to apply the MTL preparation.
wiz.node.reboot_wait_btn: Wait for the node to come back
wiz.node.reboot_waiting: rebooting, waiting for the node to come back…
wiz.skip_all: Skip configuration and go to Bobi.Studio
wiz.template.lead: The base template contains the preinstalled agent: all containers are cloned from it. Its creation is required before deploying any container (it can be done later).
wiz.template.title: LXC template (VMID 299)
wiz.videofmt.lead: Format preselected in the container deployment palette.
wiz.videofmt.title: Default video format
